short: The full BSD formula in rank $\le 1$

title.title: The full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in analytic rank $\le 1$
title.subtitle: Claim: if some $q$-power Selmer group of $E/\mathbb{Q}$ has corank 0 or 1, the exact BSD formula holds

beats.text: BSD predicts the leading coefficient of $L(E, s)$ at $s = 1$ exactly, prime by prime
The proof is a chain of release manuscripts; none is refereed or in Lean

achievement.label: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer (1965), in Tate's 1974 form
statement: \mathrm{ord}_{s=1} L(E, s) \le 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{the full BSD formula holds}
achievement.context: Before: the rank part (Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin); the exact formula only for some primes or single curves

verify.detail: Not formalized: three manuscripts totalling about 340 pages
verify.ourCheck: We read the main theorem and caveats; nothing was checked independently

sources.quote: BSD conjecture (Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer 1965; Tate 1974 formulation)
Rank part for analytic rank <= 1 known since Gross-Zagier (1986) and Kolyvagin (1988-90)
The exact formula's p-parts were known for many primes under hypotheses (e.g. Jetchev-Skinner-Wan 2017 in rank one for p >= 5), and the full formula only for specific curves checked individually.
the full Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula L^(r)(E,1)/r! = Omega_E Reg_E #Sha prod c_l / #E(Q)_tors^2 holds exactly, at every prime
the Selmer-converse paper in turn uses the release's Goldfeld/2-converse manuscript (family 006)
'Full BSD' is only the corank-<=1 case; nothing is claimed for rank >= 2.
read each family's summary and abstracts and the introduction and main theorem of every principal paper

plain: One formula ties a curve's rational points to one analytic number; this proves it exactly for rank 0 or 1

steps: Both sides of the formula are numbers built from primes
Check each prime's share on its own, with special points on the curve
Every prime matches, so the whole formula holds

voice.text: It predicts one number exactly, prime by prime. Only the rank part was known.
The proof checks each prime's share on its own, then puts them together.
Claimed: exact, in rank zero or one.
